How a Term's Block Moves Along Three Directions

Source: R/block_deriv3.R
term_block_deriv3.Rd

Returns \(\sum_{c,d,e} v_c u_d s_e\,\partial^3 X_{ij}/\partial\beta_c \partial\beta_d\partial\beta_e\), one entry per observation and column of the block: the third derivative of a term's block along three directions. The Jeffreys penalty of a block inside the term's subformula reads it in the derivative of the outer criterion.

Usage

term_block_deriv3(term, coef = NULL, v, u, s, ...)

Arguments

term

A built term.

coef

The coefficients, one per coefficient of the term, or NULL for the coefficients that the term carries.

v, u, s

Numeric vectors as long as the term's coefficients.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

A numeric matrix, one row per observation and one column per coefficient of the term.

Details

The base method returns zeros, which is exact for a block that does not move. For nl(), with \(\theta_p = h_p(Z_p\beta_p)\) and the block's column \(c\) in parameter \(p_1\), the entry is the fourth derivative of the predictor along \((e_c, v, u, s)\), the sum over the fifteen partitions of the four directions, each block of a partition carrying the derivative of one link and each partition the derivative of \(f\) of its number of blocks. Writing \(a_q, b_q, c_q\) for the three directions carried onto parameter \(q\) (\(Z_q v_q\) and so on), \(h^{(k)}_q\) for the derivatives of its inverse link and \(f_{q\dots}\) for those of \(f\), $$\begin{aligned} X^{(3)}[t,c] = Z_{p_1}[t,c]\Big[&f_{p_1}h^{(4)}_{p_1}a_{p_1}b_{p_1}c_{p_1} + h^{(3)}_{p_1}\big(a_{p_1}b_{p_1}S(c) + a_{p_1}c_{p_1}S(b) + b_{p_1}c_{p_1}S(a)\big)\\ &+ h''_{p_1}\big(a_{p_1}(Q(b,c) + R(b,c)) + b_{p_1}(Q(a,c) + R(a,c)) + c_{p_1}(Q(a,b) + R(a,b))\big)\\ &+ h'_{p_1}\big(\textstyle\sum_q f_{p_1q}h^{(3)}_qa_qb_qc_q + P(ab,c) + P(ac,b) + P(bc,a) + \sum_{q,r,s}f_{p_1qrs}h'_qa_q\,h'_rb_r\,h'_sc_s\big)\Big], \end{aligned}$$ with \(S(x) = \sum_q f_{p_1q}h'_qx_q\), \(Q(x,y) = \sum_q f_{p_1q}h''_qx_qy_q\), \(R(x,y) = \sum_{q,r}f_{p_1qr}h'_qx_q\,h'_ry_r\) and \(P(xy,z) = \sum_{q,r}f_{p_1qr}h''_qx_qy_q\,h'_rz_r\). A parameter whose development moves with the coefficients has a design of its own that moves, and its third derivative is not written: the method signals an error there.

For scs() and scte() the column \(j\) of level \(l\) is \(G_{il}W_{ij}b'(\gamma_j)\), which depends on the coefficient \(\gamma_j\) alone, so the entry is \(G_{il}W_{ij}b^{(4)}(\gamma_j)\,v_ju_js_j\), with \(b\) the map from the coefficients to the basis coefficients.

See also

term_block_deriv2(), term_block_deriv()

Examples

dd <- data.frame(x = seq(0.2, 3, length.out = 20))
dd$y <- 2 * exp(-1.3 * dd$x)
b <- term_build(nl(~ a * exp(-r * x), start = list(a = 2, r = 1.3)), dd)
dim(term_block_deriv3(b, v = c(1, 0), u = c(0, 1), s = c(1, 1)))
#> [1] 20  2
